mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs dampen economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings due to reduced sales.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months indicates disinflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary easing and improved corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200k.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it indicates robust consumer confidence and economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: When the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) and Real GDP (GDPC1) both show positive growth over the last quarter, it indicates a strong supply-side and overall economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and GDPC1 both show positive growth in the last quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both INDPRO and GDPC1 show positive growth.
